RUFINO M. ALLANIGUE Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) Member Chairman-Committee on Land Use and Zoning City of Paranaque Dear SP Member Allanigue, DILG Legal Opinion No. 11, S 2014 08 APR This has reference to your letter dated 18 November 2013 requesting the Department's legal opinion on the validity of the clauses contained in the attached ,151itte Venture Agreement (J VA) entered into between the City Government of Alltech Contractors, Inc. on 05 February 2010. In response thereto, please be advised that since the instant matter invoives a diliy approved and executed act (JVA) of the City Government of Paranaque through the ()ffice of the Mayor, then the Department is constrained to refrain from uny definitive opinion on the matter. Verily, such approved acts enjoy the prenunP12iim validity, and the Mayor is likewise presumed to have carried out his function reg.ularly in entering into the J VA, pursuant to Rule 131, Section 3 (m) of the Rules of Court. Ultimately, the validity of the J VA or any of its provisions may be determined only in a proper judicial proceeding as the issues raised in your letter are justiciable in nature, and this Department, not being a court, is not duly empowered to adjudicate on the same. In fact, pursuant to the foregoing principles, this Department had already issued Memorandum Order No. 2010-02 dated 17 September 2010 (copy attached), which provides for the guidelines on requests for legal opinions submitted to this Item numbers one (I) and two (2) of the memorandum respectively states that this Department shall not act on queries that involve and those presuupptiyely valid pets such as enacted ordinances, and consummated act! the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned. Be that as it may, you may find the ruling of the Supreme Court in the case of GSIS vs. Province of Tarlac (G.R. No. 157860, December 1, 2003) instructive, wher Couvt' emphatically declared: "where there is a perfected contract executed by the former Governor, the succeeding Governor cannot revoke or renounce the same without Che consent of the other party. The contract has the force of law between parties and they are expected to abide in good faith by their respective contractual commitments. Just as nobody can be forced to enter into a

contract, in the same manner, once a contract is entered into, no party can renounce it unilaterally or without the consent of the other. It is a principle of law that no one may be permitted to change his/her or to proceed contrary thereto, to the prejudice of the other party." We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. ly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary DILG-OUSLG
